what.text: This page follows refugees from Nigeria in all host countries combined.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 478150 Nigerian refugees, and Niger hosts the largest share, 54.0%.
Cameroon and Chad are the next largest hosts.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflict over the government of Nigeria with JAS in 2009 and from 2011 to 2025, at war level from 2013 to 2015 and in 2017.
It also records armed conflict with the Islamic State group from 2015 to 2025, at war level in most of those years.
An earlier conflict over Biafra territory is recorded from 1967 to 1970, and one with IPOB from 2021 to 2025.

when.text: UNHCR's figure rose from 51100 in 1968 to 478150 in 2025, its highest.
The main years of displacement in the data are 2018 to 2025, after big changes in each year from 2012 to 2015.
Returns to Nigeria were highest in 2024 in UNHCR's returns data.

how.text: These are year-end totals of refugees; asylum seekers from Nigeria are counted in a separate series.
People displaced inside Nigeria are counted separately by UNHCR and by IDMC, and their figures are never added.
The sources don't say which routes people took.
